'''John Michael Prausnitz''' (January 7, 1928 – November 5, 2026) was a professor of chemical engineering at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="Paz">{{cite web |last1=Rascouët-Paz |first1=Anna |title=Annual Reviews Conversations Presents An Interview with John M. Prausnitz |website=Annual Reviews |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/userimages/contenteditor/1315331682902/johnprausnitzinterviewtranscript.pdf |date=24 May 2011}}</ref><ref name="Glückliche">{{cite journal |last1=Prausnitz |first1=John M. |title=Glückliche Reise |journal=Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering |date=7 June 2019 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=1–15 |doi=10.1146/annurev-chembioeng-060718-030112 |language=en |issn=1947-5438|doi-access=free |pmid=31173520 }}</ref>

Prausnitz was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Berkeley"/> and the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to the thermodynamics of phase equilibria and its application to industrial process design.<ref name="NAE"/> In 2003, he received the [[National Medal of Science]] for his work in [[molecular thermodynamics]].<ref name="NMS"/> He developed many of the [[activity coefficient]] models used for the design of major chemical plants.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=O'Connell|first1=John P.|title=Preface to the John M. Prausnitz Festschrift|journal=Journal of Chemical & Engineering Data|date=2011|volume=56|issue=4|pages=691–693|doi=10.1021/je2000843}}</ref>

==Education==
Prausnitz was born in Berlin, Germany, on January 7, 1928. His father and his mother's stepfather were both Jewish doctors. In 1933, when the [[Nazi Party]] rescinded the [[Anti-Jewish legislation in pre-war Nazi Germany|licenses of Jewish doctors]], they were able to continue to work because they had been Frontkämpfer, "front fighters," during World War I.<ref name="Burnett"/>

In 1937,<ref name="O'Connell"/> at age 9, Prausnitz emigrated with his parents and sister to the United States, where he had an uncle in [[Lynbrook, New York]] on [[Long Island]]. His father was able to practice medicine because his German medical license was recognized by the State of New York. Prausnitz lived briefly in Lynbrook, then in Manhattan, and [[Forest Hills, Queens]]. He attended Public School 101 in New York.<ref name="Burnett"/>

In 1950, Prausnitz earned his B.Ch.E., a five-year degree, from [[Cornell University]]. In 1951, he received his M.S. in chemical engineering from the [[University of Rochester]]. He then joined [[Princeton University]] as a student of [[Richard H. Wilhelm]]. He was able to spend two summers working at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]].<ref name="O'Connell">{{cite journal |last1=O'Connell |first1=John P. |title=Preface to the John M. Prausnitz Festschrift |journal=Journal of Chemical & Engineering Data |date=14 April 2011 |volume=56 |issue=4 |pages=691–693 |doi=10.1021/je2000843 |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/je2000843 |language=en |issn=0021-9568|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
Prausnitz received his Ph.D. in chemical engineering from [[Princeton University]] in 1955 after completing a doctoral dissertation titled "Liquid-phase turbulent mixing properties."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Prausnitz|first=John Michael|url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/1529345|title=Liquid-phase turbulent mixing properties|date=1956|language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Prausnitz joined the College of Chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1955, attracted by the work of [[Joel Hildebrand]] on mixtures and by the opportunity to help shape what was then a young department.<ref name="Paz"/><ref name="O'Connell"/> Although he officially retired from teaching in the Department of Chemical Engineering in 2004,<ref name="O'Connell"/> Prausnitz remains a Faculty Senior Scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] and a Professor of the Graduate School at Berkeley.<ref name="Berkeley"/><ref name="alumnus">{{cite news |title=Alumnus Awarded Nation's Highest Science Honor |url=https://www.rochester.edu/pr/Review/V68N1/gazette4.html |work=Rochester Review|volume=68|issue=1 |publisher=University of Rochester |date=2005}}</ref>

Through his work on thermodynamics and phase behavior, Prausnitz has developed the field of [[molecular thermodynamics]], relating macroscopic properties to those of single- and multi-atom molecules. He initiated work on a number of important models for [[phase equilibria]] and the analysis of mixtures of solids, fluids, and gases, including the [[Non-random two-liquid model|NRTL]],<ref name="Heidemann">{{cite journal |last1=Heidemann |first1=Robert A. |last2=Mandhane |first2=Jamanlal M. |title=Some properties of the NRTL equation in correlating liquid—liquid equilibrium data |journal=Chemical Engineering Science |date=May 1973 |volume=28 |issue=5 |pages=1213–1221 |doi=10.1016/0009-2509(73)85030-4 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0009250973850304https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0009250973850304|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[UNIQUAC]], and [[UNIFAC]] models.<ref name="O'Connell"/><ref name="Knapp">{{cite journal |last1=Knapp |first1=Helmut |last2=Sandler |first2=Stanley I. |title=A Short History of Molecular Thermodynamics and a Tribute to John M. Prausnitz |journal=Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research |date=1 August 1998 |volume=37 |issue=8 |pages=2899–2902 |doi=10.1021/ie970776h |doi-access=free }}</ref> He is recognized for his engineering-oriented approach to molecular thermodynamics<ref name="Sanders"/> and its application to industrial process design.<ref name="NAE"/>

During his career at Berkeley, Prausnitz published hundreds of scientific papers, monographs and books detailing his theoretical and experimental work.<ref name="Knapp"/> 
In 2011, the ''[[Journal of Chemical and Engineering Data]]'' published an issue as a [[Festschrift]] in his honor.<ref name="O'Connell"/> At that time Prausnitz was credited with having published more than 760 articles, in 134 journals, with 421 different co-authors, from over twenty countries.<ref name="Burnett">{{cite web |author-first=Paul |author-last=Burnett |title=John Prausnitz: Chemical Engineering at UC Berkeley, 1955–2020 University History Interviews conducted by Paul Burnett in 2018 and 2019 |url=https://digitalassets.lib.berkeley.edu/roho/ucb/text/prausnitz_john_2020.pdf |website=Oral History Center University of California The Bancroft Library}}</ref><ref name="O'Connell"/>

He was the founding [[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering]]'', working with it from 2008 to 2018.<ref name="Doherty">{{cite journal |last1=Doherty |first1=Michael |last2=Segalman |first2=Rachel |title=Introduction |journal=Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering |date=7 June 2019 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=i–ii |doi=10.1146/annurev-ch-10-041719-100001 |language=en |issn=1947-5438|doi-access=free |pmid=31173519 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Prausnitz|first=John|date=2010-06-15|title=Preface|url=http://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.ch.052110.100001|journal=Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering |language=en |volume=1 | issue=1 | article-number=annurev.ch.052110.100001 | doi=10.1146/annurev.ch.052110.100001 | issn=1947-5438|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref> 
His books include  ''Computer Calculations of Vapor−Liquid Equilibria'' (1967),  the graduate textbook ''Molecular Thermodynamics of Fluid-Phase Equilibria'' (1969; 1986; 1999), and later editions of ''Regular and Related Solutions'' (1970) and ''The Properties of Gases and Liquids'' (1977; 1987; 2001).<ref name="O'Connell"/> 

Prausnitz was also a supporter of the Leonardo Project, an initiative to connect sciences with society, art, and philosophy, inspired by [[Jacob Bronowski]] and ''[[The Ascent of Man]]''. The project developed and shared multidisciplinary case studies, primarily for use in undergraduate classes.<ref name="Burnett"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Prausnitz |first1=John |title=Teaching Tips— Humanities and Social Relevance for Chemistry and Chemical Engineering Students: The Leonardo Project |journal=Chemical Engineering Education |date=1 August 2016 |volume=50 |issue=3 |page=175 |url=https://journals.flvc.org/cee/article/view/88293 |language=en |issn=2165-6428}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
John Prausnitz has a son, [[Mark Prausnitz]], who is a professor at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mark R. Prausnitz is Named 2023 AIChE Institute Lecturer |url=https://www.aiche.org/about/press/releases/06-06-2023/mark-r-prausnitz-named-2023-aiche-institute-lecturer |website=Press Releases |publisher=American Institute of Chemical Engineers |access-date=9 November 2023 |date=6 June 2023}}</ref>

Prausnitz died on November 5, 2026, at the age of 98.<ref>[https://www.rollinghillsmemorialpark.com/obituaries/John-Prausnitz?obId=50113838 John Prausnitz]</ref>

==Awards==
Prausnitz was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1973<ref name="NAE"/><ref name="Berkeley">{{cite web |title=John M. Prausnitz |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/cbe/pgs/prausnitz |website=College of Chemistry, UC Berkeley}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1979 for contributions to the thermodynamics of phase equilibria and its application to industrial process design.<ref name="NAE">{{cite web |title=Dr. John M. Prausnitz |url=https://www.nae.edu/28718/Dr-John-M-Prausnitz |website=NAE Website |access-date=3 March 2022}}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1988.<ref name="Berkeley"/> 

He was the recipient of many awards, from the Colburn Award of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] (AIChE) in 1962<ref name="King">{{cite news |last1=King |first1=C. Judson |title=Meet our faculty: John Prausnitz {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/meet-our-faculty-john-prausnitz |work=chemistry.berkeley.edu |date=October 20, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> to the  [[National Medal of Science]] for his work in engineering-oriented [[molecular thermodynamics]] in 2003.<ref name="Sanders">{{cite news |last1=Sanders |first1=Robert |title=Chemical engineer John Prausnitz awarded National Medal of Science |url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2005/02/16_NMS.shtml |work=newsarchive.berkeley.edu |date=16 February 2005}}</ref><ref name="NMS">{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalmedals.org/laureates/john-m-prausnitz|title=John M. Prausnitz|publisher=National Science and Technology Medals Foundation |access-date=4 October 2016}}</ref>  In 2012, he received the Lifetime Achievement in Chemical Engineering Pedagogical Scholarship, given by the [[American Society for Engineering Education]].<ref name="Wang">{{cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Linda |title=John Prausnitz Wins Lifetime Achievement Award |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |date=October 8, 2012 |volume=90 |issue=41 |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i41/John-Prausnitz-Wins-Lifetime-Achievement.html |access-date=25 May 2023}}</ref>

As of 2016, the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] renamed the Institute Lecturer Award in his honor as the John M. Prausnitz AIChE Institute Lecturer Award.<ref name="Beristain">{{cite news |last1=Beristain |first1=Kloey |title=Chemical engineering professor receives award |url=https://thebrownandwhite.com/2022/04/13/chemical-engineering-professor-receives-award/ |work=The Brown and White |date=13 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Institute Lecturer Award |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/awards/institute-lecturer-award |website=www.aiche.org |language=en |date=28 March 2012}}</ref>
